title: 1994–95 National Hurling League
text:
{{Short description|64th season of the National Hurling League}} {{Use dmy dates|date=April 2022}} {{Infobox GAA League |league = 1994–95 National Hurling League |image = |dates = 8 October 1994 – 7 May 1995 |teams = 33 |team1 = Kilkenny |captain1 = [[Bill Hennessy (Kilkenny hurler)|Bill Hennessy]] |manager1 = [[Ollie Walsh]] |titles = 9th |team2 = Clare |captain2 = [[Anthony Daly (hurler)|Anthony Daly]] |manager2 = [[Ger Loughnane]] |oneb = |two = Waterford |three = Westmeath |four = Fermanagh |previous = [[1993–94 National Hurling League|1993–94]] |next = [[1995–96 National Hurling League|1995–96]] }} The '''1994–95 National Hurling League''', known for sponsorship reasons as the '''Church & General National Hurling League''' for Church & General (later acquired by [[Allianz]]), was the 64th edition of the [[National Hurling League]], which ran from 8 October 1994 until 7 May 1995. [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] won the league, beating [[Clare GAA|Clare]] by 2–12 to 0–9 in the final.{{cite web|url=http://www.hoganstand.com/general/leagues/nhlrecords.aspx|title=National Hurling League Results 1925-2009|publisher=Hogan Stand|accessdate=18 April 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100805063526/http://www.hoganstand.com/general/leagues/nhlrecords.aspx|archive-date=2010-08-05|url-status=dead}} ==Structure== There are eight teams in each division. Each plays each other team once, home or away, and receives two points for a win and one for a draw. The top two teams in Division 1 advance to the semi-finals. The third- and fourth-placed teams in Division 1 go into the quarter-finals, as do the top two teams in Division 2. The top two teams in Divisions 2, 3 and 4 are promoted for the following season. The bottom two in Divisions 1, 2 and 3 are relegated. ==Division 1== {{Infobox football league season |competition=[[National Hurling League|National Hurling League Division 1]] |season=1994-95 |winners=[[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]]

[[Clare GAA|Clare]] and [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] joined Division 1 as the promoted teams. On 7 May 1995, Kilkenny won the title after a 2-12 to 0-9 win over Clare in the final. It was their 9th league title overall and their first since [[1989-90 National Hurling League|1989-90]].{{cite web|url=http://www.hoganstand.com/general/leagues/nhlrecords.aspx|title=National Hurling League Results 1925-2009|publisher=Hogan Stand|accessdate=18 April 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100805063526/http://www.hoganstand.com/general/leagues/nhlrecords.aspx|archive-date=2010-08-05|url-status=dead}} [[Antrim GAA|Antrim]], [[Laois GAA|Laois]] and [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] were relegated from Division 1.
